In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SD-Layer is a novel and efficient way to learn stain-specific absorption quantities in a data-driven manner.
SD-layer can be used as a front-end to any CNN architecture for medical microscopic image analysis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed SD-Layers can be affixed at the input of any CNN and can be trained end-to-end for a variety of medical imaging tasks.
the introduction of a single layer SD-Layer affixed in the front of CNNs can provide a considerable improvement to the classification performance of CNNs in medical microscopic imaging applications.
stain deconvolution is a useful pre-processing step in CNNs for medical microscopy imaging applications, and the SD-Layer is a simple and efficient method for this pre-processing step.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stain quantities are important for the performance of CNNs in microscopic imaging.
stain absorption quantities are a better feature for the classification of tissue samples than RGB intensities, as the stain absorption quantities are more tissue-specific.
the proposed SD-Layers are a general purpose front-end for all CNN architectures and can be used to improve the performance in medical microscopic imaging.
